issues.description: Blocking read loop has no timeout or liveness check; subprocess hang after first byte deadlocks parent forever
issues.detail: Once a single chunk arrives, the patch switches the fd to blocking mode and enters an unbounded `while True: os.read()` loop with no timeout, no poll, no signal handling, and no check_process_exited guard. If the writer subprocess writes one chunk then stalls, hangs, or fails to close its FIFO end (deadlock, crash mid-write, fd leaked to grandchild, GC pause), the parent blocks indefinitely. The patch trades an intermittent JSONDecodeError for a deterministic hang — the original code's bounded-wait postcondition is silently abandoned.

issues.description: check_process_exited / macOS empty-events EOF fallback deleted without justification
issues.detail: The removed branch encoded a documented macOS quirk: poll returns no events, read returns empty, but the writer has exited and content is present — return it. The patch replaces this with `pass`, on the unproven assumption that control always reaches the blocking-mode path. If the first read hits BlockingIOError (now also a no-op `pass`) or poll fires with zero data, the loop never enters blocking mode and the deleted exit condition is precisely the one that would have saved it. On macOS or under load this regresses a real platform invariant.

issues.description: fcntl mode switch is not exception-safe and never restored
issues.detail: `fcntl.fcntl(fifo_fd, F_SETFL, flags & ~O_NONBLOCK)` mutates kernel state on a file descriptor whose lifetime extends beyond this function, with no try/finally to restore O_NONBLOCK. If the blocking read raises (EINTR, EIO, OSError, signal), or if the caller reuses the fd, the descriptor is silently left in blocking mode. The fd's blocking discipline is part of its contract with the surrounding IPC machinery; a reader helper should not mutate that contract as a hidden side effect.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler reduced to bare `pass`, removing its only useful behavior
issues.detail: Previously, BlockingIOError with content present meant 'writer closed, we're done — break.' The new code just passes. On platforms that raise BlockingIOError instead of returning empty (exactly the case the old comment documented), the loop now busy-loops on poll forever instead of exiting. Combined with the removed process-exit check, this strips the reader of a key termination signal. Either delete the except entirely with justification, or restore the break-on-content semantics — do not leave a no-op except as a trap for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Two-phase state machine has no stated contract, invariant, or documentation
issues.detail: The function now operates in two distinct phases (non-blocking poll until first byte, then blocking drain until EOF) with two different time models, two different EOF disciplines, and one shared fd and accumulator. No docstring, comment, or invariant explains the mode switch, why blocking termination is guaranteed, or which phase governs the `timeout` parameter. Callers cannot tell whether timeout still bounds total wait time (it does not — after first byte it is irrelevant). Decompose into named helpers (wait_for_first_chunk, drain_until_eof) or write the two-phase contract into a docstring, including preconditions on the writer set.

issues.description: POSIX blocking-read guarantee cited without stating its preconditions
issues.detail: The commit message and inline comment claim blocking read returns 0 'ONLY after writer closes AND all kernel pipe buffers are drained — POSIX guaranteed.' True only when exactly one writer ever held the write end and it has close(2)d its only write fd. FIFOs can have multiple writers; subprocess fork/exec can leak the write fd to grandchildren. Additionally, if the actual root cause is writer-side Python buffering (as the PR description suggests), the right fix is on the writer (flush + close, unbuffered I/O, or length-prefixed framing) rather than papering over on the reader. State the precondition or fix the correct side.

issues.description: No regression test for the race the patch claims to fix
issues.detail: This is a concurrency patch addressing an intermittent ~86KB truncation race, and the diff contains zero tests. A small unit test with a writer that writes >PIPE_BUF, closes, and exits between the parent's poll and read — exercising both the poll-timeout-with-content and BlockingIOError-with-content paths — would lock in the fix and catch the deleted-behavior regressions identified above. Without a deterministic test, the next refactor reintroduces the original bug silently.

issues.description: Control flow is nested and harder to read than the bug it fixes
issues.detail: The function now has an outer while, inner try, inner-inner `while True` with break, an else branch that does nothing, and an except that does nothing — two `pass` branches as visible scar tissue from the deleted logic. Refactor the post-first-byte path into a small helper (`_drain_blocking(fifo_fd)`) and let the outer loop's intent stay legible. Good taste: eliminate the special case, do not bury it under nested loops.

issues.description: Magic 8192 read size repeated without justification
issues.detail: Both the non-blocking and the new blocking read use a bare literal 8192. Neither is named, documented, or tied to PIPE_BUF. Once committed to blocking mode, a larger buffer (e.g., 64KB) would materially cut syscall count with no latency downside. Name the constant (e.g., CHUNK_BYTES) with a one-line justification, or revisit the size for the blocking phase.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diagnosis is correct — non-blocking reads can race with writer close while kernel FIFO buffers still hold bytes, and a POSIX blocking drain is a legitimate primitive — but the implementation trades an intermittent truncation bug for a deterministic hang. Two P0 issues dominate: the inner blocking loop has no timeout, poll, or process-exit check, so a stalled writer wedges the parent forever; and the deleted macOS check_process_exited fallback (along with the now-neutered BlockingIOError branch) removes the very escape hatches that protected the non-happy paths. Secondary issues cluster around an unsafe and unrestored fcntl mode flip, an unstated two-phase contract, an over-broad POSIX-guarantee claim that ignores writer-set preconditions, and the absence of any regression test for a concurrency fix. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK. Required changes: preserve poll-based liveness (or a deadline) inside the blocking phase, restore O_NONBLOCK in a try/finally, restore or replace the process-exit / BlockingIOError exits, document the two-phase contract, and add a deterministic test for the writer-exits-with-buffered-data interleaving.
